label: rem:content-scaling-dictionary
title: Box content as the isospin dictionary for the Bethe--Weizsäcker scaling functions
html:
The mass model reads the content c of a box as an isospin label and assigns to each content class a Bethe--Weizsäcker scaling function. This assignment is a dictionary of the model, not a consequence of the proposition it interprets: the proposition fixes c as the q-Jucys--Murphy eigenvalue exponent, a total-spin datum of the sub-tower, and the table below is the model's choice of what that datum counts.

Content c Isospin meaning Scaling f_c(Z,N)
+1 proton nearest-neighbor Z(Z{-}1)/A^{1/3}
-1 neutron nearest-neighbor N(N{-}1)/A^{1/3}
0 balanced (pn mixed) A^{2/3} or \pm 1/\sqrt{A}
\pm 2 next-nearest same-type Z^{4/3}/A^{1/3}
\lvert c\rvert \geq 3 long-range T^p(T{+}1)^p/A^p

Each scaling function counts the number of nucleon pairs the model places at content c in the nuclear ground state. The content is not a magnetic quantum number of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) weight space V_\lambda: for a two-row shape (a,b) the number of boxes a+b never equals the number of weights a-b+1, and for a+b \geq 3 the largest content a-1 exceeds the largest weight (a-b)/2, so no box-to-weight assignment realises the older reading of this table.
